Alright, let me think about this year on my 5 mu...

---

**My thinking (as the farmer):**

Five mu isn't much — my husband works in town most of the year, so the fields are mostly mine and the children's grandmother helps when she can. I've been doing wheat-maize for 20 years now, same as everyone in the village. I don't change much because what works, works.

**For the wheat:**
I'll plant in early October, like always, after the maize comes off. I usually buy seed from the agro-shop in town — Jimai or whatever variety they have, costs maybe 4-5 yuan a jin. I save a little of my own seed too as backup but the bought seed comes up better.

For fertilizer, I put down two bags of compound fertilizer (45% NPK) per mu before plowing — that's about 50 jin, maybe 25 kg. Then around jointing in March, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I top-dress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu. My neighbor old Wang's wife uses more, but I can't afford to buy that much, and honestly her yield isn't that much better than mine.

Irrigation — I'll water in winter once (December, the "freezing water" — it's important so the roots survive), then again at jointing in spring, and maybe once more at grain-filling if it's been dry. Three times usually. The well water costs money, the electricity adds up. If May has rain I skip the last one.

I spray weeds once in spring with the small sprayer. For aphids, I check at heading time — sometimes I spray, sometimes not.

I expect maybe 800 jin per mu, that's 400 kg. A good year 900 jin, a bad year 700.

**For the maize:**
The week the wheat comes off in mid-June is crazy busy. I hire the man with the no-till seeder from the next village — costs about 30 yuan per mu but saves me from plowing, and I have to get the maize in within a few days or I lose growing time. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu type, whatever the shop has, about 4 yuan per mu of seed actually since I plant at the right density.

Fertilizer for maize — I put it all in at planting through the seeder, one shot. Maybe 30 kg of compound per mu. Some farmers top-dress at the big trumpet stage but I don't bother, my plot is small and the labor is too much. I know I lose a bit of yield but it's fine.

Irrigation — usually one time after planting if there's no rain, then maybe one more in August at tasseling. Summer has more rain so often I only water once.

Spray for armyworm if I see them. Herbicide goes on right after planting before the maize comes up.

Maize yields better than wheat, maybe 1000 jin per mu (500 kg) in a normal year.

**Money-wise:**
The whole year on 5 mu, inputs come to maybe 1800-2000 yuan total. Both crops together I might clear 2500-3000 yuan after selling — really not much. The off-farm work is what feeds the family. The land is more for our own grain and because it's our land, you don't leave it empty.
